nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_000
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What potential benefit does the introgression of climate-adaptive alleles from Ae. tauschii provide for wheat?
nodes.answer: It has the potential to improve wheat performance under water-limiting conditions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: According to Qureshi et al. (2013), what global ramifications can drought in Australia cause?
nodes.answer: Drought in Australia can cause significant global food price spikes in wheat, meat, and dairy.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What effect does a low dose of gamma radiation have on maize according to the study?
nodes.answer: A low dose of gamma radiation (50 Gray) induces cytogenetic changes, enhances drought tolerance, and improves yield characteristics in maize.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are some documented effects of gamma radiation on plants?
nodes.answer: Documented effects of gamma radiation on plants include changes in cellular structure and metabolism, dilation of thylakoid membranes, variation in photosynthesis, modulation of the antioxidant system, and accumulation of phenolic chemicals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the impact of low-dose ionizing irradiation on plants?
nodes.answer: Low-dose ionizing irradiation on plants can result in accelerated cell proliferation, increased germination rate, enhanced cell growth, improved enzyme activity, greater stress resistance, and higher crop yields.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What were the two groups of treatments in the simulated drought experiment?
nodes.answer: The two groups of treatments were one exposed to seven doses of gamma irradiation with distilled water, and the other exposed to the same doses of radiation along with simulated drought stress using 10% polyethylene glycol (PEG).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: In what way can slow vascular plant species facilitate bryophyte survival during dry periods?
nodes.answer: Slow vascular plant species, being well-adapted to drought, can provide a moister microclimate in summer, thus facilitating bryophyte survival during dry conditions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: In what way does drought impact the taste of grapes, and how are vineyards coping with this challenge?
nodes.answer: When a certain temperature threshold is exceeded, grapes stop photosynthesizing to retain water, affecting their taste. Vineyards are facing constant warming of growing season temperatures and limitations on groundwater pumping for irrigation to overcome water deficits.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Drought-resistant crop varieties_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the observed effect of drought on P. pinea and P. nigra trees?
nodes.answer: P. pinea trees over 100 years old show a negative effect of drought, while P. nigra experienced a cumulative negative effect of drought across all ages.
